summary: Neo Delay in Stereo mode: the first track's Length becomes Sync and Feel (or a free Time), Feedback carries over to ±99 %, the filter in the loop becomes Neo Delay's low cut (highpass) or high cut (lowpass), Dry thru and Wet out a crossfade and an output gain.

rules.why: Lengths count in Length unit: ticks (the default) are Buzz's whole samples per tick, so the echo follows the tempo; a length in ticks that is a note value (1 tick = 1/16 at 4 ticks a beat, 3 ticks = 1/8 dotted, 6 = 1/4 dotted …) becomes Neo Delay's Sync and Feel, which follow the tempo too; any other length, and lengths in ms or samples, a free Time at the song's tempo and rate.
Both in % of each echo fed back (its source: buf = in + fb · filter(buf)); Neo Delay's stops at ±99 %.

bandreject.note: its notch is about 100 Hz wide (measured at 1 kHz, 4.4 dB deep on a third octave); Neo Delay has none, so the echoes keep that band.

rules.why: Its filter sits in the loop, on every echo (its source's DoWork), as Neo Delay's do; measured on one echo at 1 kHz, each type a second-order Butterworth (dsplib's DSP_BW_Init*): its high-pass is Neo Delay's low cut exactly; its low-pass is Butterworth where Neo Delay's high cut has two real poles (a softer knee: −8.5 dB an octave up against −12.4); its band-pass is about 100 Hz wide, narrower than Neo Delay's cuts can make, so it has no counterpart (the filters open, with a note); its band-reject's notch is left out.
Dry thru (on or off) and the echoes at Wet out (raw/128) add; Neo Delay crossfades them and sets the output's level.

remarks: NiNjA dElaY is mono: ReBuzz gives it left + right summed (+6 dB for a centred sound, taken on the output connections so the line keeps the input's level); Neo Delay in Stereo mode keeps the input's image.
Each of its tracks is a tap of its own with its own filter (up to 8); Neo Delay has one: the first track's settings move.
Its Max Delay attribute (1 s by default) caps its lengths; the mapping doesn't read attributes.
